articles.title: Republicans ready for ‘very hasty’ ‘Trump-a-palooza’ convention in Texas
articles.summary: The Republican National Committee’s (RNC) first-of-its-kind midterm convention has been cloaked in mystery until a few weeks ago. Details are finally emerging about what’s expected to be a two-day pep rally to bolster hype and encourage Republicans to get out the vote in November amid President Trump’s shrinking approval rate. But some Republicans are quietly…
articles.body:
The Republican National Committee’s (RNC) first-of-its-kind midterm convention has been cloaked in mystery until a few weeks ago. Details are finally emerging about what’s expected to be a two-day pep rally to bolster hype and encourage Republicans to get out the vote in November amid President Trump’s shrinking approval rate .

But some Republicans are quietly frustrated that the event came together so fast and at such a high price tag for lawmakers: House members are reportedly expected to contribute $25,000 to attend.

A GOP operative told The Hill that while Trump has touted the convention for a year, candidates and incumbents have not had long to plan.

“Lot of things made this very hasty that didn’t need to happen,” the operative said. Trump announced at the end of June that the convention would be in Dallas on Sept. 9 and 10.

The midweek convention also conflicts with the first two NFL games of the season and bumps against the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks, raising questions about whether the “ Trump-a-palooza ” will get enough airplay to justify the expense.

And while primetime addresses from Trump and Vice President Vance could gin up excitement as Texas Republicans defend their toss-up Senate seat , the convention risks pulling candidates in other states off the campaign trail during a critical summer stretch.

“I think the big question on people’s minds is whether or not this is helpful,” said Joshua Blank, research director for the Texas Politics Project at the University of Texas at Austin, pointing to the program’s polls that show Trump’s approval rating underwater in the state.

Blank also looked back to 2018, when Democrats were rallying around Beto O’Rourke in his campaign to oust Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas). Trump, then in his first term, visited Texas to boost Cruz, but “most analyses after the fact tended to indicate that that visit didn’t really help Cruz,” he said.

“It raises the question of whether the timing is somewhere between ill-conceived or just not conceived at all,” Blank added of the event scheduling. “This may be convenient for some, but it doesn’t seem to be necessarily timed for maximum impact. It seems more like a reaction to concerns about enthusiasm among Republican voters. It’s more of a reaction than it is a clear plan.”

But Texas Republican consultant Brendan Steinhauser contended that “it’s a net positive” for the GOP in Texas and beyond.

“It’s two days. It’s not two weeks … so you’re not really taking away from anything else,” he said. “Texas is indeed competitive, and this makes all the sense in the world to me,” he said. “As long as it’s a net positive financially, and they make use of the time and deliver a message, then I think it’s a good thing.”

Texas Republican strategist Vinny Minchillo argued that “people are digging really hard to find problems with the event,” which he sees as a good opportunity to rev up the the GOP base in Texas as they look toward a Senate race that’s “much tighter than anybody would really like on the Republican side.”

“Certainly, conflicting with an NFL game early in the season is going to be tough,” Minchillo said, but he argued that the conflict won’t eclipse the convention’s purpose as a “rally-the-troops event and an opportunity for fundraising.”

“The people who want to watch the president are going to watch the president, and maybe the people who want to watch the NFL game are just going to record the president and watch him later,” he added.

The major news networks have not said whether they will show coverage of the convention. A spokesperson for Fox News confirmed the network would broadcast some coverage, but the details have yet to be announced. About 20,000 people are expected to attend, according to John Hiller, White House aide and the CEO of the convention’s organizing board.

Meanwhile, Dallas’s city agencies are quickly preparing to secure the event. The Dallas Police Department (DPD) held a press conference with officials from the FBI and Secret Service Thursday afternoon, confirming that security needs would cost the city $1.8 million.

“The city is also actively evaluating reimbursement and grant opportunities and will pursue all eligible funding sources to help offset the costs to Dallas taxpayers,” City Manager Kimberly Bizor Tolbert said. “At the same time, reimbursements do not necessarily determine whether we provide necessary public safety services.”

Deputy Police Chief Devon Palk said people will experience public transit and road closures as well as an increased law enforcement presence, including officers from other agencies that are not the DPD. Palk and Bizor Tolbert both said they expect protests related to the convention.

The cost comes after Bizor Tolbert announced spending restrictions this spring as the city veered toward a potential budget shortfall of more than $30 million for the fiscal year.

“We’ve got a city that’s got budget problems, and the city of Dallas has a lot of financial issues. So $2 million is not an insignificant amount of money for them to spend,” Minchillo said. “But that’s what it costs to bring in these big events.”

Dallas Mayor Eric Johnson, a longtime Democrat who switched to the GOP in 2023 and now helms the Republican Mayors Association, has said hosting the landmark midterm event is a “ tremendous honor .” Dallas is the largest U.S. city with a Republican mayor.

The RNC has announced 109 items and speakers for the two-day event, most of which are to be announced. Vance is set to give a keynote on the first night, and Trump will close out the second night.

“The president’s personality is a big one, and he’s the leader of the party right now, and I think he’ll have — it’ll be Trump imagery and gear everywhere. … But I think that there will be a lot of excitement for other candidates as well and opportunities to support them,” Steinhauser said.

“It’ll be not only Trump-a-palooza, but it’ll be a big event for the whole ticket. And if not, that would be a missed opportunity.”

Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) and House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) are among the top GOP figures expected to attend , as is Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, who’s locked in the Lone Star State’s high-stakes Senate race against Democrat James Talarico.

“They’re going to Texas, obviously, because they’re trying to help Paxton win the Senate race,” said Jon Taylor, a University of Texas at San Antonio political science professor. Trump held a fundraiser for the RNC, with Paxton in attendance, in late August.

But the convention also comes amid controversy over the Trump administration’s plans for border wall construction inside Texas’s Big Bend National Park and frustration over Trump’s embrace of data center builds that have prompted Paxton and Gov. Greg Abbott (R) to support restrictions — which could hamper efforts to energize Republicans in the state.

“I know the president thinks that somehow … he’ll be able to energize the Republican base, MAGA base. I’m not convinced of that, to be honest. I mean, I’m wondering how much airtime they’re going to give both to Ken Paxton in particular, but to Greg Abbott as well, and how much of this is just going to be essentially just about Donald Trump,” Taylor said.

articles.title: This week on the Hill: House aims to pass measure to avert shutdown ahead of midterms
articles.summary: The House is back in session this week after a monthlong August recess, with lawmakers aiming to avert a government shutdown before funding expires Sept. 30 amid the 2026 election season. The biggest item on the agenda will be a Senate-passed stopgap measure, also known as a continuing resolution (CR), that would keep the government…
articles.body:
The House is back in session this week after a monthlong August recess, with lawmakers aiming to avert a government shutdown before funding expires Sept. 30 amid the 2026 election season.

The biggest item on the agenda will be a Senate-passed stopgap measure, also known as a continuing resolution (CR), that would keep the government funded through Dec. 11. The Senate passed the measure 90-6 earlier this month, sending it to a House that had previously passed its own stopgap bill extending funding through Dec. 4.

The bill is expected to have both GOP and Democratic support.

Rep. Rosa DeLauro (D-Conn.), the ranking member of the House Appropriations Committee, said in a statement earlier this month that the measure is a “clear improvement” over the House-passed stopgap measure.

The Senate remains out of session and is not scheduled to return until Sept. 14, leaving several top Republican priorities in limbo, including a third reconciliation bill, the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) and a farm bill.

The House may also take up a measure this week to censure Rep. Chuck Edwards (R-N.C.) after the House Ethics Committee found his conduct with two young staff members had violated “the spirit” of the chamber’s rules against sexual harassment.

Meanwhile on the campaign trail, Massachusetts is expected to be in the spotlight as incumbent Sen. Ed Markey (D-Mass.) and Rep. Seth Moulton (D-Mass.) go head-to-head in the Senate Democratic primary on Tuesday.

Six candidates are also vying for the Democratic nomination for Massachusetts 6th Congressional District, a seat that Moulton currently represents and is rated “Solid Democrat” by the nonpartisan Cook Political Report.

House to hold vote on CR: The Senate-passed stopgap funding measure is expected to advance through the lower chamber.

House to consider socialism resolution: The House will consider a resolution condemning socialism in all its forms.

House could take up Edwards censure: The lower chamber could take up a resolution to censure Edwards over sexual harassment allegations.

Markey and Moulton face off: Markey, 80, is hoping to retain his seat, while Moulton, 47, has been arguing for generational change.

Six candidates battle in Democratic primary: The race will determine who will advance to the general election to represent Massachusetts 6th District.

House to take up Senate stopgap funding measure

House GOP leaders are aiming to put the Senate CR on the floor under a fast-track process known as suspension of the rules, which requires two-thirds majority support for a measure to pass.

The Senate version of the CR was negotiated with Democrats and passed the upper chamber overwhelmingly — a signal that neither party is interested in risking a shutdown just before the midterms.

The CR contains a provision to temporarily halt a rule from the White House budget office that would give political appointees in the executive branch more authority over dispersing federal grants — language that might not bode well with some House Republicans.

Still, the measure is expected to pass the lower chamber with broad bipartisan support.

“This bill is a clear improvement over the House Republican continuing resolution, but we are still nearly two months away from the end of the fiscal year and should be working together to pass full-year funding bills that lower the cost of living, rein in the corruption at the highest levels of the government, and can earn the support of Democrats and Republicans in the House and in the Senate,” DeLauro said.

Rep. Randy Fine (R-Fla.) previously told The Hill that he needs to look at the Senate CR “a little bit more closely to understand the differences. But my understanding is that the bills are not so far apart that we won’t be able to get to an answer.”

Asked about whether he was confident Republicans will get a CR across the finish line, Fine said, “I’m very confident about the CR because the Senate has passed one. So while they’re not the same, the fact that they have interest in doing it, and we have interest in doing it, makes me optimistic we’ll get something over the finish line.”

The stopgap measure comes as the House has only passed three out of the 12 appropriations bills needed to fund the government.

Both Democratic and Republican appropriators in the Senate, meanwhile, remain deadlocked over topline spending levels, and the upper chamber has not yet passed any of the 12 annual appropriations bills before the September deadline.

House to consider resolution condemning socialism

The House Rules Committee will meet Monday to consider a GOP-backed resolution that would condemn and denounce “socialism in its all forms, including the Democratic Socialists of America, and opposes the implementation of socialist policies in the United States.”

The resolution comes as a string of progressive Democrats — some of whom are members of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) — have won congressional primaries across the country.

House Republicans have hammered the democratic socialists, arguing that their ideas are radical and would only drive up the cost of living and make it harder for Americans to make ends meet.

The resolution also calls for the enactment of the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility (SAVE America) Act, which requires proof of citizenship to register to vote in federal elections and the presentation of an ID to cast a ballot.

House could take up a resolution censuring Edwards

The lower chamber may take up a resolution this week to censure Edwards, after the House Ethics Committee said it found his conduct with two young staff members had violated “the spirit” of the chamber’s rules against sexual harassment and unwanted advances and recommended he be formally censured by the full House.

That conduct included bringing one staffer on a trip to New York City that lasted an extra day for his birthday and included extra activities like a helicopter ride and Broadway show; writing poems for a staffer and crying during a slideshow at her going away office party; telling a staffer he left early from an event because she brought a date; sending personal texts late in the evenings; paying for massages and spa treatments for the staffer; and paying for a singer to go to a staffer’s birthday party to sing Ed Sheeran’s “The Hills of Aberfeldy” and saying it was “from a special someone.”

Edwards issued a letter to colleagues last week denouncing the Ethics Committee report. In his letter, he wrote that there are no House rules prohibiting members of Congress and staff from being friends, spending social time together or “genuinely and deeply caring” about each other.

“Those distinctions matter. Otherwise, perfectly permissible conduct can become evidence of wrongdoing simply by accumulating enough examples of it and assigning them an improper motive,” the letter reads.

“Ten permissible acts do not become misconduct merely because they are placed together in ten paragraphs,” it continues.

Edwards has already dropped his bid for reelection, but Rep. Kat Cammack (R-Fla.) previously said the House should follow through on censuring him.

Markey and Moulton face off in Senate primary

The Massachusetts Senate Democratic primary will feature a tough contest between Markey and Moulton.

Moulton has framed the race around generational change while questioning Markey’s progressive bona fides. He’s suggested the Massachusetts senator has not done enough to fight back against the Trump administration and advance priorities like the Green New Deal.

“I’m running against the senator’s decision after 50 years in Washington, to run for another term at age 80,” the congressman said in a final debate. “I believe in a new generation of leadership. I believe we can do better than the status quo.”

Moulton has garnered support from Democrats like New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill and Reps. Derek Tran (Calif.), Chrissy Houlahan (Pa.), Seth Magaziner (R.I.) and Pat Ryan (N.Y.).

Markey, meanwhile, has railed against his attacks, pointing to his central role in authoring the climate-oriented policy while seeking to tie the congressman to past votes and statements on everything from the Iran war to transgender rights. He’s also noted that he received endorsements from key progressives including Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.).

“If you pass the torch to Congressman Moulton, you’re going to get burned. Massachusetts deserves better than a Senator who throws trans kids under the bus and uses public office as a personal self enrichment fund,” Markey wrote on social media last week.

Polling has shown Markey comfortably leading Moulton in the contest. The winner of the September primary will be the heavy favorite to win the Senate seat in the Bay State come November.

Six candidates vie for Democratic nomination

The crowded Democratic primary for Moulton’s seat in Massachusetts’s 6th Congressional District is shaping up as a wide-open contest, with six candidates from varied professional and political backgrounds vying for the nomination ahead of the Sept. 1 primary.

The field includes Bethany Andres-Beck, a software engineer; John Beccia, a business leader; Jamie Belsito, a former state representative; Dan Koh, a former White House and Boston City Hall official; Mariah Lancaster, a veterinarian and former science policy advisor in the U.S. House; and state Rep. Tram Nguyen.

Koh has perhaps the strongest name recognition in the field, thanks in large part to his experience in the Biden administration. He served in several senior roles under former President Biden, including as deputy assistant to the president and deputy director of the White House Office of Intergovernmental Affairs, after previously serving as chief of staff to then-Labor Secretary Marty Walsh.

He has received endorsements from Biden, former Vice President Kamala Harris and former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg.

But Beccia has also been garnering the attention of voters, as he frames himself as a political outsider who will bring a fresh new perspective to Congress.

“Washington insiders write the rules, trade on them, and then promise to fix the system on their way in. It’s time to end that,” Beccia wrote on social media earlier this month.

Caroline Vakil, Emily Brooks, Ashleigh Fields and Julia Mueller contributed to this report.

articles.title: Markey trounces Moulton in Massachusetts Senate primary poll
articles.summary: Sen. Ed Markey (D-Mass.) is handily leading Rep. Seth Moulton (D-Mass.) in a primary race for his seat in the upper chamber, according to a new poll. In the Emerson College Polling poll, 60.4 percent of respondents that are likely to vote in the Democratic primary or have already voted said that they would back…
articles.body:
Sen. Ed Markey (D-Mass.) is handily leading Rep. Seth Moulton (D-Mass.) in a primary race for his seat in the upper chamber, according to a new poll.

In the Emerson College Polling poll, 60.4 percent of respondents that are likely to vote in the Democratic primary or have already voted said that they would back Markey if the primary were that day, while 32.8 percent said they would back Moulton. The poll found 6.7 percent of the same group undecided.

Earlier this month, Moulton and Markey battled it out during the final Massachusetts Democratic Senate primary debate. The House member is running a long-shot campaign to oust the senator, a progressive, in the primary this Tuesday.

Moulton, 47, has centered the race around generational change and questioned the progressive bona fides of Markey, an 80-year-old. The representative has suggested the senator hasn’t done enough to battle the Trump administration and push priorities such as the Green New Deal.

Markey, meanwhile, has noted his central role in writing the Green New Deal. He has also tried to tie Moulton to past votes and statements on issues like the Iran war and transgender rights.

Polling has often leaned in Markey’s favor. The winner of the primary will likely take the Senate seat in the fall.

The Boston Globe announced that it was endorsing Moulton against Markey in recent weeks . The editorial board for the paper said Moulton “is promising that he can bring new vision and vigor to an aging, ailing, and deeply unpopular Democratic Party.”

“It is true that Markey still looks and sounds sharp, and that he brings much valuable experience to the table,” the board wrote. “But this is no ordinary time.”

The Emerson College Polling poll took place from Aug. 28 to 29, featuring 550 respondents and a credibility interval of plus or minus 4.1 percentage points.

articles.title: Presidenciáveis criticam emendas parlamentares, mas apostam em propostas genéricas, diz estudo | G1
articles.standfirst: Estudo da Transparência Internacional Brasil aponta que candidatos reproduzem soluções genéricas, reclamam do volume de indicações, mas não tentaram solucionar problema quando passaram pelo parlamento e governos estaduais.
articles.summary: Estudo da Transparência Internacional Brasil aponta que candidatos reproduzem soluções genéricas, reclamam do volume de indicações, mas não tentaram solucionar problema quando passaram pelo parlamento e governos estaduais.
articles.body:
Os planos de governo dos candidatos à Presidência da República apresentados ao Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) focam em propostas genéricas para as emendas parlamentares, que são alvos de investigação da Polícia Federal (PF) e do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF).

A avaliação é de um estudo da ONG Transparência Internacional Brasil, que acompanha a execução desses recursos, que só neste ano prevê R$ 61 bilhões para serem executados conforme indicação de deputados e senadores.

O levantamento indica ainda que, apesar das críticas ao sistema, os candidatos ao Palácio do Planalto pouco avançaram no modelo de definição de verbas do Orçamento enquanto ocuparam cargos públicos.

🔎 As emendas parlamentares são um montante do Orçamento reservado para serem executados conforme a indicação dos congressistas para seus redutos eleitorais. Por meio delas, os deputados e senadores podem direcionar verbas para obras, compra de equipamentos, custeio de serviços e investimentos em estados e municípios de suas bases eleitorais.

“Nenhum candidato propõe um reequilíbrio dos poderes e responsabilidades. Se os parlamentares vão controlar recursos do Orçamento e indicar diretamente os beneficiários dessas verbas, eles precisam ser responsabilizados em caso de desvios”, afirma Guilherme France, Gerente do Núcleo de Incidência e Litigância Estratégica da Transparência Internacional Brasil.

France destaca que o descompasso atual em que parlamentares têm muitos poderes, mas nenhuma responsabilidade, “é a senha para que deputados e senadores continuem a inflar esses recursos ano após ano, até que o Poder Executivo não passe de um laranja do orçamento público” (leia mais abaixo).

A rastreabilidade e a transparência na indicação e execução das emendas parlamentares estão no centro de decisões do ministro do STF Flávio Dino, relator de uma ação sobre o tema .

Por ordem do Supremo e ainda de indicações do Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU), a PF analisa a destinação desses recursos reservados por mais de 90 parlamentares, diante das suspeitas de irregularidades.

A ONG Transparência Internacional Brasil comparou as propostas sobre o tema apresentadas pelos seis candidatos melhores colocados nas pesquisas. Os planos de governo são protocolados na Justiça Eleitoral junto com o registro de candidatura.

Lula, Flávio, Renan, Caiado, Cury e Zema. — Foto: Reprodução

➡️O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), candidato à reeleição, e Renan Santos (Missão) não abordaram a transparência e rastreabilidade dos recursos.

Lula fala em enfrentar uma “grave distorção” na elaboração do Orçamento e diz que as emendas “sequestraram” a peça orçamentária.

O presidente diz ainda que o volume de recursos indicados por parlamentares, que consomem cerca de um quinto do total disponível para o governo investir, dispersam a distribuição do montante e reduzem a eficiência, além de dificultar a renovação do Legislativo em todas as esferas.

Em 2022, Lula não mencionou o tema, mas durante a campanha criticou as emendas do relator, que ficaram conhecidas como “Orçamento Secreto” e acabaram vetadas pelo Supremo.

➡️Já Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) sugere mais transparência, controle e rastreabilidade às emendas parlamentares, “priorizando sua alocação em políticas públicas prioritárias do Plano Plurianual, aprovado pelo parlamento”.

O candidato, que é senador, foi responsável pela destinação de quase R$ 300 milhões entre 2020 e 2026 e não apresentou nenhum projeto de lei sobre o tema no parlamento.

➡️Renan Santos faz uma menção genérica sobre “mudanças nas emendas” e defende o fortalecimento fiscal de municípios, que ficariam menos dependentes do “clientelismo” perpetuado pelos repasses de parlamentares.

➡️Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) defende uma mudança na relação orçamentária entre Executivo e Legislativo, mas propõe soluções também consideradas genéricas pelo estudo, como:

identificar autoria, beneficiário final, objeto, custo e andamento físico;

integrar prioridades parlamentares ao planejamento nacional;

impedir que a fragmentação do orçamento inviabilize políticas estruturantes.

Caiado defende ainda pactuar com o Congresso critérios de planejamento, transparência, manutenção, custo total e resultado, com o objetivo de reduzir a pulverização e impedir que recursos “escassos sejam destinados a objetos sem capacidade de operação”.

➡️Já o candidato Romeu Zema (Novo) defende a redução de recursos destinados à indicação de parlamentares no Orçamento, mas não define qual seria o valor ideal.

“Racionalizar o uso das emendas parlamentares: limitar as emendas parlamentares a um percentual reduzido do orçamento discricionário e condicionar sua destinação ao cumprimento de critérios objetivos de interesse público e transparência, evitando a fragmentação do orçamento em projetos de baixo impacto ou com finalidade meramente eleitoral”, diz o plano de governo.

Zema foi governador de Minas Gerais de 2019 a março de 2026. Atualmente, o estado tem o maior valor do orçamento destinado às emendas parlamentares: R$ 2,5 bilhões em 2026.

➡️Augusto Cury não menciona o tema em seu programa de governo.

Políticas públicas x interesses eleitorais

O gerente do Núcleo de Incidência e Litigância Estratégica da Transparência Internacional Brasil afirma que as emendas deveriam atender a políticas públicas estruturais, mas acabam sendo guiadas pelos interesses eleitorais dos parlamentares, que pulverizam a aplicação do dinheiro.

Como resultado, a União acaba se envolvendo em questões locais, como a pavimentação de ruas, construção de quadras e praças e pagamento de funcionários de postos de saúde.

“E isso a União não faz bem, tem dificuldade de controlar e acaba gerando desperdício e corrupção. Além da pulverização, prejudica o processo de implementação das políticas públicas a ausência de critérios técnicos na distribuição dos recursos”, afirmou.

France diz que outro problema é que municípios que não necessariamente precisam de tantos recursos acabam recebendo os maiores volumes, o que aprofunda a desigualdade regional no Brasil.

Segundo ele, o tema aparece de forma superficial nos programa de governo porque os candidatos parecem não saber o que fazer com a questão.

“É um tema muito impopular com a população que as vê associadas a escândalos e desvios, mas é praticamente uma unanimidade entre a classe política. Então nenhum candidato parece querer desagradar as bases de seus partidos, mas deixam sinalizações para o eleitorado de que vão fazer reformas pontuais”.

France ressalta o fato de que nenhum candidato a Presidente promete acabar com as emendas parlamentares.

“Não deixa também de ser um reconhecimento da perda de poder do Executivo frente ao Legislativo”.

O especialista diz ainda que o aumento da fatia de recursos destinado a emendas parlamentares deveria estar atrelado a despesas obrigatórias da União e não à Receita Corrente Líquida, como atualmente.

“No ritmo que está, em breve, as emendas parlamentares consumirão todo o orçamento da União. E não só da União – como isso tem se repetido nos estados e municípios, o mesmo se observará em todos os níveis da federação”.

articles.title: O que faz um deputado estadual? | G1
articles.standfirst: Entenda quais são as funções dos parlamentares, que representam o Poder Legislativo nos estados. O g1 detalha as atribuições de cada um dos cinco cargos em disputa no pleito de 2026.
articles.summary: Entenda quais são as funções dos parlamentares, que representam o Poder Legislativo nos estados. O g1 detalha as atribuições de cada um dos cinco cargos em disputa no pleito de 2026.
articles.body:
Votação para deputado estadual simulada em urna eletrônica — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

O deputado estadual é o representante da população no Poder Legislativo de cada estado. Ele é eleito para um mandato de quatro anos, sem limite para reeleição, e tem como principais funções elaborar e votar leis estaduais, fiscalizar as ações do governo estadual e analisar o orçamento do estado .

Eles são eleitos pelas populações dos 26 estados e do Distrito Federal -- onde são chamados de deputados distritais, e exercem a mesma função legislativa.

Os deputados estaduais atuam nas Assembleias Legislativas, onde discutem e votam projetos que tratam de temas de competência dos estados . Também podem:

propor mudanças na Constituição Estadual;

apresentar projetos de decreto legislativo e de resolução; e

analisar propostas enviadas pelo governador, pelo Judiciário, pelo Ministério Público e pelo Tribunal de Contas.

Outra atribuição é fiscalizar a aplicação dos recursos públicos e a atuação do Executivo estadual . Para isso, podem convocar secretários de Estado para prestar esclarecimentos, realizar diligências em órgãos públicos, acompanhar políticas públicas e solicitar informações sobre ações do governo.

Os parlamentares também analisam e aprovam o orçamento anual do estado , que define como serão distribuídos os recursos públicos em áreas como saúde, educação, segurança e infraestrutura. Além disso, votam as contas do governador, após parecer do Tribunal de Contas do Estado.

Os deputados estaduais ainda participam de comissões permanentes e temporárias, responsáveis por discutir projetos específicos antes da votação em plenário. Também podem propor a criação de Comissões Parlamentares de Inquérito (CPIs) para investigar possíveis irregularidades na administração pública.

Além da atividade legislativa, o deputado estadual atua como representante da população, recebendo demandas de cidadãos, entidades e lideranças locais e encaminhando pedidos ao governo estadual .

‼️ Embora tenham poder para criar leis estaduais, os deputados não podem legislar sobre temas de competência exclusiva da União, como direito penal, direito eleitoral e relações exteriores . Além disso, não podem criar leis que neguem, em alguma instância, a Constituição Federal.

Em contrapartida, podem propor normas sobre assuntos de interesse estadual, como organização da administração pública, tributos estaduais, transporte intermunicipal e funcionamento das polícias civis e de outros órgãos estaduais.

articles.title: Fim da 6x1 e taxa das blusinhas: Congresso define pautas de Lula | G1
articles.standfirst: Congresso não está de recesso, mas as atividades pararam desde o começo do processo eleitoral. Nessa semana, os parlamentares diminuem compromissos de campanha para votações.
articles.summary: O Congresso Nacional vota o fim da escala 6x1 e a taxa das blusinhas em esforço concentrado antes das eleições e do recesso parlamentar de novembro.
articles.body:
Na última semana de votações no Congresso Nacional antes das eleições de 2026, os parlamentares devem avançar em pautas prioritárias para o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), que busca a reeleição.

🔎 O Congresso não está de recesso, mas as atividades parlamentares praticamente pararam desde o começo do processo eleitoral. Nesse período, os parlamentares devem diminuir os compromissos de campanha para votar os temas.

A partir desta segunda-feira (31), os projetos devem ser votadas tanto nas comissões quanto nos plenários de Câmara dos Deputados e Senado Federal . Depois dessa semana, os parlamentares só retornam para Brasília em novembro.

Um dos focos do governo será a Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) do fim da escala 6x1, que tramita no Senado Federal. A PEC entrou em pauta depois de o presidente da Casa, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), ter retomado diálogo com Lula. (Veja os demais)

Em 21 de agosto, Alcolumbre enviou a proposta para a Comissão de Constituição e Justiça do Senado, depois de quase três meses de espera do governo.

Agora, governistas pressionam para votar tanto na CCJ quanto no plenário a PEC do fim da 6x1 no mesmo dia, nesta segunda. No entanto, depois de um almoço com Lula e o presidente da Câmara, deputado Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB), Alcolumbre não garantiu que isso vá acontecer.

Entre os senadores, a expectativa é de que, se o fim da 6x1 chegar ao plenário, o texto será aprovado, ainda mais com a proximidade das eleições. O relator, senador Omar Aziz (PSD-AM), manteve o texto assim como ele saiu da Câmara.

O presidente da República, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT)(c), entre os presidentes do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União Brasi-AP)(e), e da Câmara dos Deputados, Hugo Motta (Republicanos- PB), durante a cerimônia de assinatura da medida provisória da reforma do setor elétrico, no Palácio do Planalto, em Brasília (DF), nesta quarta-feira, 21 de maio de 2025. Pelas regras propostas, beneficiários da Nova Tarifa Social de Energia não vão pagar contas de luz com faixa de consumo de até 80 kWh. A mudança foi anunciada pelo Ministério de Minas e Energia (MME). — Foto: Wilton Junior/Estadão Conteúdo

Além da redução da jornada de trabalho, o Congresso vai analisar outros temas considerados estratégicos pelo governo Lula. São eles:

Medida provisória (MP) que acabou com a taxa das blusinhas;

Regulamentação da exploração de minerais críticos e terras raras; e

O Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Data Center (Redata).

A MP que acabou com a chamada taxa das blusinhas, o imposto de importação de 20% sobre compras internacionais de até US$ 50, foi publicada em maio e tem até 8 de setembro para ser aprovada ou rejeitada pelo Congresso.

Com as novas regras, o ministro da Fazenda passou a ter a competência para alterar as alíquotas do imposto de importação das remessas postais internacionais, inclusive reduzindo a zero a tributação de até US$ 50.

Caso a votação não ocorra, o imposto voltará a ser cobrado em 9 de setembro. Apesar disso, o fim da taxa já conta com acordo entre Lula, Motta e Alcolumbre.

A comissão responsável por analisar a MP deve votar o tema na terça-feira (1º). No dia seguinte, a expectativa é que os plenários da Câmara e do Senado votem a medida.

Já a PEC da Segurança Pública ainda precisa ser votada na CCJ do Senado antes de chegar ao plenário. A votação também deve ser realizada na quarta-feira (2), depois de ficar parada seis meses no Senado.

O relator da proposta, senador Rogério Carvalho (PT-SE), apresentará relatório favorável à PEC, sem alterações em relação ao texto da Câmara, para agilizar a aprovação e consequente promulgação. Lula já afirmou que, após a aprovação, vai criar o Ministério de Segurança Pública.

Já o Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Datacenter (Redata) deve ir direto ao plenário. O Redata é uma política para incentivar a instalação de datacenters no Brasil.

Esse tipo de instalação reúne servidores, sistemas de armazenamento e equipamentos de rede para processamento de dados em grande volume.

A Política Nacional de Minerais Críticos cria uma legislação específica para atrair investimentos nacionais para o setor, com um fundo de R$ 5 bilhões. O projeto já foi aprovado na Câmara em maio e aguarda somente a votação no Senado.

🔎 Minerais críticos e estratégicos são cobiçados pela indústria e diplomacia mundial, isso porque, dentre eles, destacam-se as chamadas terras raras, grupo de 17 elementos químicos essenciais para o funcionamento de uma série de produtos.

Entre eles estão o lítio, o cobalto, o níquel e o grafite, fundamentais para baterias de veículos elétricos, turbinas eólicas, painéis solares e semicondutores.

articles.title: O que faz o presidente? | G1
articles.standfirst: Entenda quais são as funções do chefe do Poder Executivo nacional. Série de vídeos do g1 explica os principais temas das eleições de 2026 e tira dúvidas.
articles.summary: Entenda quais são as funções do chefe do Poder Executivo nacional.
articles.body:
Em outubro, os brasileiros vão escolher quem vai governar o país pelos próximos quatro anos. O presidente da República comanda o Poder Executivo nacional e tem entre suas atribuições definir as políticas públicas nacionais, escolher os ministros, criar ou extinguir ministérios e decidir para onde vai o orçamento nacional.

Também cabe ao presidente representar o país no exterior, sancionar ou rejeitar projetos de lei aprovados no Congresso, escolher os indicados para cargos relevantes para a República, como ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) e o Procurador-Geral da República (PGR) -- que dependem de aprovação do Senado. Veja mais detalhes no vídeo acima.

📍Em uma série de 50 vídeos, o g1 vai explicar os principais temas das eleições de 2026. Os conteúdos mostram como funcionam as pesquisas, explicam o papel dos cargos em disputa e o funcionamento do Congresso, e trazem orientações práticas para votar. A série também aborda o impacto das novas tecnologias na campanha, como inteligência artificial, deepfakes e influenciadores.

articles.title: Registro de candidaturas: TSE julga Lula, Zema e Flávio Bolsonaro | G1
articles.standfirst: Processos que atestam regularidade de candidaturas de Lula, Romeu Zema e Flávio Bolsonaro serão julgados até 2 de setembro no plenário virtual. Registro de Renan Santos foi adiado por suspeitas de irregularidade.
articles.summary: O TSE inicia a análise do registro de candidaturas de Lula, Zema e Flávio Bolsonaro, enquanto o pedido de Renan Santos foi adiado por suspeitas de irregularidade.
articles.body:
O Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) começa a julgar nesta segunda-feira (31) os pedidos de registro de candidaturas dos postulantes à Presidência e Vice-Presidência da República.

Os processos estão em análise no plenário virtual da Corte e os julgamentos vão até 2 de setembro. Nessa primeira leva de processos nem todos os registros de candidaturas serão analisados. Estão na pauta os pedidos de registro de:

Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e Geraldo Alckmin (PSB) - relator André Mendonça;

Samara Martins (UP) e Raquel Brício (UP) - relator André Mendonça;

Romeu Zema (Novo) e Eduardo Girão (Novo) - relator André Mendonça;

Hertz Dias (PSTU) e Vanessa Portugal (PSTU) - relator André Mendonça;

Edmilson Costa (PCB) e Cleusa Santos (PCB); relatora Estela Aranha;

Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Alfredo Gaspar (PL), relatora Estela Aranha.

Além do Requerimento de Registro de Candidatura (RCC), que é individual, os ministros julgam também o Demonstrativo de Regularidade dos Atos Partidários (Drap) das legendas ou coligações.

Por isso, também constam na pauta processos sobre a regularidade da coligação de Lula, “Brasil Pronto para Mais”, além dos procedimentos relacionados à regularidade do Novo, UP, PSTU, PCB e PL.

Urna eletrônica para votação nas eleições brasileiras — Foto: Marcelo Camargo/Agência Brasil

O registro de candidatura é o pedido individual de cada candidato. Nele, a Justiça Eleitoral verifica as condições de elegibilidade, a documentação pessoal, eventuais causas de inelegibilidade e os demais requisitos para que aquela pessoa possa concorrer.

Já o Drap analisa se o partido ou a federação seguiu corretamente as regras para apresentar candidatos.

É por meio dele que são informados dados sobre a convenção partidária, a escolha dos candidatos, a composição da chapa e o cumprimento das exigências legais para lançamento das candidaturas.

A relação do Drap com o registro de candidatura é de dependência. Se o Drap é negado, isto é, se a Justiça conclui que houve irregularidade nos atos partidários, os registros individuais dos candidatos vinculados a ele tendem a ser prejudicados.

O ministro Dias Toffoli, relator do Drap do Missão e do pedido de registro de Renan Santos à Presidência da República, adiou o julgamento do processo do candidato .

A análise também começaria nesta segunda no plenário virtual, mas Toffoli retirou o processo da pauta diante de “indícios de ilicitude”.

Toffoli apontou possíveis irregularidades em razão do descumprimento da legislação eleitoral que obriga os candidatos a informarem todas as contas nas redes sociais utilizadas nas campanhas no momento de registro da candidatura.

O ministro afirmou em despacho que Renan e seu vice, Aroldo Medina, apresentaram 18 contas nas redes sociais em documentos enviados à Corte em 19 de agosto. Entretanto, no pedido de registro feito dia 7, o candidato havia divulgado apenas uma conta na rede social X e um site.

articles.title: g1 promove debates com candidatos ao Senado em 8 estados e no DF | G1
articles.standfirst: Encontros serão realizados ao longo de setembro, com transmissão ao vivo no g1 e nos perfis do g1 no YouTube, no TikTok e no Instagram. Primeiro será realizado em Pernambuco, na quarta-feira (2).
articles.summary: Encontros serão realizados ao longo de setembro, com transmissão ao vivo no g1 e nos perfis do g1 no YouTube, no TikTok e no Instagram.
articles.body:
Cenário do debate montado na redação da Globo no Recife, em Pernambuco. — Foto: g1

O g1 promove, pela primeira vez, debates com candidatos ao Senado . Serão encontros em oito estados — São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Minas Gerais, Pernambuco, Ceará, Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul e Piauí — e no Distrito Federal, ao longo do mês de setembro.

Neste ano, cada estado e o Distrito Federal vão eleger dois senadores , para renovar 54 das 81 vagas da Casa. A eleição será em 4 de outubro.

Os debates terão formato de vídeo vertical e serão transmitidos ao vivo no g1 e nos perfis do g1 no YouTube, no Instagram e no TikTok. Depois, a íntegra de cada programa ficará disponível no g1 e no YouTube.

Todos os debates terão o modelo de banco de minutos: em vez de blocos com tempos fixos definidos previamente para perguntas e respostas, cada candidato administra o próprio tempo ao longo do programa, decidindo quando usá-lo para apresentar propostas e interagir com os demais participantes.

Cada candidato terá 15 minutos de fala ao longo do debate. Além disso, haverá um minuto para as considerações finais.

O debate gira em torno de temas, sem a obrigação de que os candidatos façam perguntas uns aos outros.

A dinâmica funcionará da seguinte forma: todos os candidatos ficarão sentados diante de uma mesa redonda, junto com o mediador. Eles poderão falar olhando diretamente para câmeras posicionadas à sua frente.

A transmissão exibirá a imagem e o som de apenas uma pessoa por vez. Mesmo que os candidatos falem simultaneamente, só terá a imagem transmitida quem estiver com a palavra no momento.

Serão chamados os candidatos de partidos e federações com representação mínima de cinco parlamentares no Congresso Nacional.

Também serão convidados candidatos dos demais partidos que alcancem ao menos 5% de intenções de voto na última pesquisa Quaest ou Datafolha divulgada antes de cada debate.

Pernambuco 2 de setembro, às 14h Mediação de Marcio Bonfim

Mato Grosso 3 de setembro, às 13h (14h de Brasília) Mediação de Gleyce Santos

Mato Grosso do Sul 4 de setembro, às 12h (13h de Brasília) Mediação de Alex Mendes

Minas Gerais 8 de setembro Mediação de Sérgio Marques

Distrito Federal 11 de setembro Mediação de Antônio de Castro

Ceará 21 de setembro Mediação de William Santos

Rio de Janeiro 22 de setembro Mediação de Edimilson Ávila

São Paulo 25 de setembro Mediação de Ana Paula Campos

Piauí 25 de setembro Mediação de Marcos Teixeira

A série de debates integra a cobertura especial das Eleições 2026 realizada pela Globo. A iniciativa reforça o compromisso de oferecer informação de qualidade, ampliar o conhecimento dos eleitores sobre os candidatos e contribuir para um debate público qualificado sobre temas de interesse dos estados e do país.

articles.title: The US-Canada trade war in 5 charts
articles.summary: The US-Canada trade war is being felt on both sides of the border.
articles.body:
The US and Canada appear no closer to resolving their ongoing trade dispute.

Tensions have been simmering between the two neighbours since President Donald Trump returned to the White House just over 18 months ago, and unleashed a wide-ranging global programme of tariffs.

Canada was one of the first countries the Trump administration hit with levies, and is one of two countries to respond with its own reciprocal measures.

Currently, the US has hit Canada's key sectors of steel, aluminium, lumber and automobiles with tariffs, and last week imposed an additional 50% levy on about C$28bn ($20bn; £15bn) of Canadian goods.

Canada has hit back with its own counter-tariffs on American goods, announcing on Tuesday what it calls a "dollar-for-dollar" and "strategic" retaliation designed to match the US tariffs.

With no resolution in sight, how has this enduring trade war affected Canada and the US, and what could come next?

Here are five charts to help break it all down.

The tariffs and counter-tariffs have hit some states and provinces harder than others.

In Canada, some provinces have been more exposed to US sectoral tariffs on steel, steel derivatives, aluminium, and autos and vehicle parts that don't comply with the current North American trade deal, known as the USMCA.

Ontario, the most populous province with a significant manufacturing sector, has been hardest hit by the auto and steel tariffs.

Several Ontario auto parts and assembly plants have announced layoffs and production cuts, and the province is estimated to have lost tens of thousands of manufacturing jobs since early 2025.

Metal exports from Quebec - which produces steel, copper and aluminium - fell 36% between February 2025 and 2026, and there was a 3.6% drop in employment in the sector, according to data released in July.

The Royal Bank of Canada estimates that Ontario and Quebec are the most impacted by US sectoral tariffs, while Newfoundland and Labrador, New Brunswick, Alberta, Saskatchewan and Prince Edward Island are the least exposed.

Additional US tariffs on $20bn worth of Canadian goods that came into effect on 22 August are expected to impact all provinces in some way, though British Columbia, Quebec and Ontario will feel the brunt.

The US economy is much larger and the impact of Canada's counter-tariffs won't be as stark.

But some states will feel the pain of Canada's retaliation more than others, with tariffs levied on C$28bn worth of US goods from steel to furniture, cosmetics and toilet paper, as of 8 September.

According to data by Statistics Canada, the swing state of Ohio will be hardest hit, with C$3.2bn - or 12% - of its exports soon to be tariffed by Canada, followed by Illinois and Pennsylvania.

For Ohio, it's the tax on steel that will particularly hurt, as well as the tax on laundry machines. In Illinois, where farm equipment giant John Deere is based, it will be the new tariffs on farm and construction equipment.

Derek Holt, an economist with Scotiabank, noted that Canada's counter-tariffs appear to be "very deliberately oriented" towards some swing states that could decide the US balance of power in the upcoming midterm elections.

From the lowest tariff rates to one with the pack

Prime Minister Carney has assured Canadians that, despite the high-profile trade fight, they face some of the lowest US tariff rates compared to other countries.

But with the latest 50% tariffs imposed on a range of Canadian goods, the average effective US tariff rate on Canada is now higher than Mexico's, and is approaching the rate faced by others like the UK and Vietnam.

An average effective tariffs rate reflects the average tariff paid across all imports.

According to data by the Royal Bank of Canada , the average effective US tariff rate on Canada in June was 2.9% - the lowest among major US trade partners. It has now nearly doubled to 5.7%.

By comparison, the US effective tariff on the UK is 6.2%. China still faces the highest US tariffs at an average of around 20.5%.

Canada, by the happenstance of being neighbours with the world's largest economy, is hugely reliant on US trade.

Their proximity - and free trade agreements in place since the 1980s - has allowed the two countries to develop one of the world's most deeply economically integrated trading relationships.

The US buys more than 70% of Canadian exports, and is a top US trading partner alongside Mexico and China.

But the tariff fight has already started to shift Canadian businesses to other markets. Carney has pledged to double Canada's non-US exports over the next decade.

Bank of Canada statistics suggest that Canadian firms are exporting more to countries other than the US since Trump's return to the White House in January 2025.

Some businesses are adapting to find customers elsewhere.

Matteo Sgaramella, who owns Toronto-based menswear clothing company Outclass, told the BBC he has started attending trunk shows in Paris instead of New York, helping him reach more customers in Europe.

"The reception has been amazing," he said, adding that some European stores are particularly enthused about supporting Canadian products due to the ongoing trade war with the US.

"We're kind of seen as the one country that's kind of standing up to the Americans right now," Sgaramella said.

Other businesses, however, are struggling to diversify their trade, particularly in Ontario manufacturing sectors that are deeply integrated with the US.

A recent report by the Canadian Chamber of Commerce pointed out three such regions in Ontario - Oshawa, London and Kitchener-Cambridge-Waterloo - as being particularly vulnerable.

"These cities remain heavily tied to the US market, while growth in exports outside the US has been limited or insufficient to offset broader weakness in trade activity and local economic conditions," the report said.

While some businesses are lagging, foreign direct investment into Canada hit C$96.8 billion in 2025, the highest inflow of capital to the Canadian economy since 2007.

Canada's economy also strongly rebounded in the second quarter of 2026 to 3.3% growth in the country's GDP, thanks to a jump in exports and domestic investment.

These latest figures have warded off recession concerns, at least for now.

Carney is hoping to attract even more investment. In September, his government will host the first-ever Canada Investment Summit, bringing major investors, CEOs and business leaders to Toronto for two days.

On both sides of the border, tariffs have hit jobs and disposable income.

According to an analysis commissioned by Canadian American Business Council (CABC), if the US and Canada allow the USMCA to fail, there would be tens of thousands of jobs lost, primarily in the manufacturing industries directly affected by tariffs and that are highly reliant on the US market.

Around 55,000 manufacturing jobs have already been lost in Canada from January 2025 to January 2026, according to Bank of Canada data.

Not all figures are bad, however, as employment has steadily risen in Canadian sectors that are not vulnerable to US tariffs.

But there is a risk of further Canadian job losses due to the recent 50% tariffs imposed by the Trump administration.

Calgary-based economist Trevor Tombe estimates that a total of 90,000 jobs across Canada could be lost if these new US tariffs persist.

In the US, the non-partisan Center for American Progress estimates that Trump's "Liberation Day" tariffs, placed last year on dozens of America's trade partners, have also led to tens of thousands of jobs lost manufacturing, transportation and warehousing sectors.

Even for those whose jobs remain secure, the tariffs have meant higher sticker prices on everyday items.

The US-based Tax Foundation estimates that an American household could pay $840 more on average this year due to Trump's tariffs on a number of nations, including Canada.

Canada's counter-tariffs are much more targeted and are designed to limit the impact on Canadian consumers, but economists say businesses will likely now pay more to manufacture goods, as a bulk of the taxes will be applied on industrial supplies imported from the US.

articles.title: Approximately 15 people may be missing after Grand Canyon flash flood: Parks service
articles.summary: Approximately 15 people may be missing or unaccounted for after a significant flash flood occurred in the Grand Canyon, the National Parks Service (NPS) said Sunday. The flood ripped through Bright Angel Canyon and the Phantom Ranch area on Saturday, the Grand Canyon National Park’s communications office said in a release. The Bright Angel Trail…
articles.body:
Approximately 15 people may be missing or unaccounted for after a significant flash flood occurred in the Grand Canyon, the National Parks Service (NPS) said Sunday.

The flood ripped through Bright Angel Canyon and the Phantom Ranch area on Saturday, the Grand Canyon National Park’s communications office said in a release . The Bright Angel Trail is the most popular hiking trail into the Grand Canyon, per the NPS .

National park staff and the Arizona Department of Public Safety are “continuing evacuation and response efforts and working to account for individuals who may have been in the affected area,” the release added.

“The NPS also asked anyone who knows of hikers or backpackers who were in the inner canyon along the Bright Angel Creek corridor,” the communications office noted.

“This includes individuals who may have been traveling along the North Kaibab Trail from the North Kaibab Trailhead to Phantom Ranch, staying at Bright Angel Campground, or traveling or staying in the area known as ‘the Box’ north of Phantom Ranch.”

The flash flood began at approximately 2:30 p.m. PCT and resulted in “significant impacts to infrastructure” throughout Bright Angel Canyon, the national park said in an initial Sunday release .

“Nearly all footbridges spanning Bright Angel Creek were destroyed, eliminating hiker access across the creek. Grand Canyon National Park staff are continuing to assess damage to trails, bridges, utilities, facilities and other infrastructure,” the park’s communications office added.

The park also noted on Saturday that the Black and Silver bridges crossing the Colorado River, Phantom Ranch, Bright Angel Campground, the Phantom Ranch Canteen and cabins, as well as the entire North Kaibab Trail from the North Kaibab Trailhead to Phantom Ranch, were closed until further notice.

As of Sunday morning, authorities had evacuated 62 individuals from Phantom Ranch and the lower North Kaibab trail, with additional individuals scheduled to be evacuated later in the morning from Cottonwood Campground and Phantom Ranch. The national park reported zero injuries as of Sunday morning.

Authorities are transporting evacuees to the Maswik Lodge Cafeteria, the national park noted in the initial Sunday release.

David Gregory told CNN he was hiking with a small group when the floods hit, with officials evacuating them via helicopter to a local high school and setting them up in a hotel room for the night.

“We realized the creek near camp was black with debris and flowing rapidly,” Gregory told CNN.

In a third release on Sunday, the park’s communications office said all park concessions were halting overnight lodging, including the Maswik Lodge, while the park will remain open for day use.

The NPS is encouraging those who know anyone who may have been hiking or backpacking in the aforementioned areas to contact its Investigative Services Branch Tip Line and provide any information about the individual — including their name, approximate location, travel plans, group size, clothing or backpack description or when they were last known to be in the area.

More than 409,000 people visited the Grand Canyon last month, and more than 2.4 million had done so this year as of the end of July, according to NPS data .
